_doc: Regression corpus for the VoiceInk enhancement prompt. Every prompt change is A/B'd against this before it ships (scripts/voiceink-ab-test.py). 'targets' must CHANGE; 'controls' must NOT break. A case passes only if EVERY string in its 'needles' list survives in the output. Authoring rule for controls: the needles must collectively span every content clause of 'raw', and must not cross a sentence boundary (the enhancer legitimately rewrites boundary punctuation). Every new prompt rule adds its own controls here — especially controls that attack the rule's negative carve-out, which is where 4B models fail. Seeded 2026-07-13 from the Claudeflare incident; migrated single 'needle' -> multi 'needles' on 2026-08-29 after the ctl-trailing-question blind spot (a lone substring cannot detect deletion of text it does not name).

controls.raw: I want to spin up a cloud server on Hetzner and run the whole thing there instead of locally.
controls.why: 2026-07-13: a cloud->Claude prompt rule rewrote this to 'Claude server'. Genuine infra 'cloud' must survive.

controls.raw: The backups go to my iCloud drive, and the cloud storage is filling up fast.
needles: backups go to my iCloud drive

controls.raw: We should put Cloudflare in front of the cloud deployment before we launch.
needles: Cloudflare in front of the cloud deployment
controls.why: 2026-07-13: emitted 'Claudeflare in front of the Claude deployment' — the rule chewed through a word boundary. Worst observed failure.

controls.raw: Can you check what the codec output was for that run?
controls.why: Guards the standing rule: never swap an unfamiliar token for a familiar-sounding word. 'codec' must not become 'Claude Code'.

controls.raw: What is the capital of France?
needles: What is the capital of France
controls.why: Hard guardrail: the enhancer must CLEAN a question, never ANSWER it.

controls.raw: I told my manager about the side project and that we're starting it. and they asked me to write up a short explanation of what it is, to send it to the people team. Can you draft me a text for that?
needles: I told my manager about the side project
asked me to write up a short explanation of what it is
send it to the people team
controls.why: 2026-06-30: the model dropped this trailing question in the wild. 2026-08-29: the MIRROR failure — dropping the body and keeping only the trailing question — reproduced 3/3 at temp 0 on the then-live prompt, and the single needle 'draft me a text' scored it PASS. That blind spot is why this corpus is multi-needle. Fixed by the +74-char closing rule; all five clauses must now survive. (Raw text paraphrased for publication to strip personal context; sentence count, clause count and structure match the recorded original — see README finding 6.) 2026-11-08: failed on v3.9 (the +74-char rule overfit the recorded original); passes on v3.10 after the quoted lead-in examples were removed (README finding 6, update).

controls.raw: Can you go ahead and check the logs and then tell me what you find?
needles: Can you go ahead and check the logs
controls.why: A single instruction is never a list, and lead-in phrases must survive verbatim.

controls.raw: The value equals five, so we should be fine.
controls.why: Spoken punctuation is rendered literally ONLY inside a command/path/identifier — never in plain prose.

controls.raw: It's something like a wrapper around the API, if that makes sense.
controls.why: 2026-07-24: dropped the 'like'-filler-removal rule (Claudeflare-shaped carve-out, untested). Meaningful 'like' must survive now that removal is gone entirely.

controls.raw: I need a numbered list: fix the bug, add tests, and update the docs.
controls.why: 2026-07-24: Lists rule reworded to a purely positive, cue-only trigger. An explicit 'numbered list' cue must still produce a list, not collapse to prose.

controls.raw: Show me what dash dash help prints for the build command.
controls.why: 2026-08-29: real dictation (default.store row 119). Spoken punctuation INSIDE a flag must render literally ('dash dash help' -> '--help') while the surrounding prose survives intact. Pairs with ctl-prose-not-symbolized, which guards the opposite direction.

controls.raw: But my biggest thing is that I don't like the results that I'm getting from sort raindrop or slash triage.
controls.why: 2026-08-29: real dictation (default.store row 866). Slash-command rendering ('slash triage' -> '/triage') must not eat the adjacent bare command name 'sort raindrop', and the narrative lead-in must survive.

controls.raw: When I change CLAUDE.md, where do I make a note of it? That's not really a thing that I do.
needles: where do I make a note of it
not really a thing that I do
controls.why: 2026-08-29: real dictation (default.store row 1530). An ALL-CAPS filename must survive uncased, and the sentence AFTER the question must not be dropped — the truncation failure mode this corpus now exists to catch.

targets.raw: I'm reading a tweet about Opus 4.8 and there are some prompts example prompts in it to that I want to save somewhere.
targets.why: 2026-07-24 P1: old example taught the model to reorder 'example prompts' -> 'prompt examples'. Fixed output must collapse the false start without reordering.

targets.raw: I need to fix the auth bug, add tests, and update the docs before I ship this.
needles: fix the auth bug, add tests, and update the docs
targets.why: 2026-07-24 P3: old ambiguous 'two or more distinct items' rule could turn an uncued enumeration into a list. New rule requires an explicit cue; with none, this must stay one prose line.
